comments.body:
# Validation: does the Gerrit code-review gate achieve accumulated attestation for stacked stories?

Scenario validated (user ask): epic with stories A, B, C. Agent RED reviews+lands approval for A, agent BLUE for B (separate worktrees, both based on main), agent GREEN builds C on top of combined A+B and wants (1) a review of only C's delta, (2) a combined landing carrying attestations for all three, (3) no large re-review of A+B+C combined at merge time.

## Verdict: PARTIALLY ACHIEVED — the per-change delta review works; attestation accumulation breaks at the "combine A+B" step, by deliberate design.

Evidence base: epics dowdy-swear-bird (b744), alto-fruit-punch (d251), smoky-flare-slug (1fa8); session logs slap-tripe-vat, watery-fray-waltz, vivid-mull-need; stories bluff-crane-pixel (S3), cogent-strut-kid (S4b), low-cloud-wreck (WS1), virid-trench-stone (WS6), van-withe-folly (WS6-b), weedy-lath-abbey (WS7); ADR 0013; infra/gerrit/project.config, infra/compose/gerrit.config, infra/gerrit/replication.config, infra/gerrit/webhooks.config; src/rebar/review_bot/ (voter.py, gerrit_client.py, adapter.py, reconcile.py, app.py); src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py, src/rebar/llm/code_review/assemble.py.

## What WORKS
1. Review-of-delta-only: the bot reviews each change's own parent-relative diff (GET /a/changes/{id}/revisions/{rev}/patch = format-patch vs parent; gerrit_client.py). For stacked change C with parents A<-B, the reviewed diff is C's delta only, while clone_change_ref materializes the full tree (incl. unmerged A+B) for detector/file-tool context. GREEN's goal (1) is fully met.
2. Per-change attestation + atomic landing: submit requirement `label:LLM-Review=MAX AND -has:unresolved` evaluates per change; submitWholeTopic=true lands a multi-change feature atomically (proven live: changes 22/23, S3 AC4). Chain submit from the top also works (stock Gerrit, per-change gates all enforced). Goal (2) is met as a chain/topic of three individually-attested commits — NOT as one squashed change (a squash is a new change with no votes => full combined review, i.e. the exact thing to avoid).
3. No combined mega-review ever runs: the bot has zero chain/topic awareness (voter._extract reads only change+patchset ids); every review is per-change delta-scoped. Goal (3)'s literal fear ("large re-review of A+B+C combined") cannot happen.

## What BREAKS
4. The combine step wipes votes. A and B were built as siblings on main; combining them requires rebasing B onto A (new patchset for B). copyCondition = changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE only — TRIVIAL_REBASE was DELIBERATELY excluded (S3 "peer-pattern correction"; ADR 0013: "a rebase always re-triggers review"; red-team flag: copying across a moved base "would certify a tree the LLM never reviewed"). So B's +1 is dropped at assembly; the webhook auto-triggers a fresh FULL four-pass review of B's (delta-scoped) new patchset. Cost: N-1 re-reviews to assemble N sibling stories; plus nondeterministic risk the re-review casts -1 with new findings that GREEN (not BLUE) must remediate.
5. Cascade on any base motion: if main advances (or A is amended to address a finding), the whole stack above must rebase => all descendant votes wipe => per-change re-reviews down the chain. Standard Gerrit also refuses submitting a child based on an outdated ancestor patchset, forcing exactly this rebase.
6. Semantic tension in the goal itself: B's +1 certified B-on-main, not B-on-A. Accumulation across a base move is unsound as specified — the current design chose soundness (re-review) over accumulation. Any fix must address the interaction review, not just carry the vote.
7. No accumulation record in rebar: no "code-review" attestation kind exists (only plan-review / completion-verifier); the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar is only emitted when target_ticket is supplied and the Gerrit voter supplies none. The volatile Gerrit label is the sole artifact.
8. Residual unknowns: project submit type is unset in-repo (inherits All-Projects, presumably MERGE_IF_NECESSARY) => history shape of a chain submit on GitHub main is unpinned; outdated-ancestor + topic-union submit mechanics undocumented. The open epic smoky-flare-slug AC4 already records "carry vs re-run across trivial rebases" as an undesigned question for the future Verified vote.

## Design-intent finding
The multi-agent stacked-worktree scenario was never designed: "stacked diffs" appears once in slap-tripe-vat's research-basis list; rebar search "stacked"/"relation chain" has zero Gerrit design hits. The shipped mechanism for multi-story features is topics (atomic landing), and the shipped no-re-pay lever is copyCondition NO_CODE_CHANGE (message-only amends). Everything else re-reviews.

## Options to close the gap (not actioned)
A. Workflow discipline (no code): build stories as a chain from the start (BLUE stacks on A, GREEN on B) under one rebar-<feature> topic; votes survive until main moves. Tradeoff: serializes agents, defeats independent worktrees; still cascades on amend-of-ancestor.
B. Add changekind:TRIVIAL_REBASE to copyCondition: cheap, restores accumulation for byte-identical rebases. Tradeoff: reopens the red-team hole (certifies a tree never reviewed against its new base) — rejected once already.
C. Interaction-scoped re-review on TRIVIAL_REBASE: carry nothing, but replace the full four-pass re-review with a narrowed "does this delta still hold on the new base" pass — mirrors the plan-review epic boil-golem-veto's narrowed delta-re-review story (grace-thud-feint). Middle ground: sound + cheap; new capability to build.
D. Pin the submit strategy + document the chain/topic convention for epics in CONTRIBUTING.md (independent hygiene regardless of A-C).

# Addendum: 5-requirement re-evaluation + OSS-validated pattern recommendation

User pinned 5 core requirements: (1) never review a huge diff in one review; (2) accumulate a huge feature off-main, land it all at once; (3) every change reaching main passed LLM review; (4) no invalidation fragility from content-comparison or merge/rebase instability; (5) pattern must be OSS-validated, not novel/Frankenstein. Note (4)+(5) eliminate the prior options: TRIVIAL_REBASE vote-carry IS content comparison; a custom narrowed interaction re-review IS a novel invention; current chain+topic fails (4) (rebases wipe votes).

## Recommendation: Gerrit server-side feature branches + reviewed merge change (the OpenDev-documented pattern)

Stories = small reviewed changes targeting refs/heads/feature/<name>, merged into the branch AS they pass (attestation consumed immediately into branch history — no vote ever needs to survive a rebase; branch history is the durable accumulator, not label state). Feature completion = one --no-ff merge commit of the branch into main, pushed to refs/for/main as its own reviewed "merge change", gated by the same submit requirement, submitted atomically. No rebases anywhere → requirement 4 by construction.

## OSS validation (web-research agent, 2026-07-01, URLs in agent report)
- OpenDev/OpenStack: Infra Manual documents the exact flow (server-side branch via UI; pushMerge ACL; git merge --no-ff + push refs/for/master). LIVE: openstack/swift feature/mpu + feature/threaded active 2025-2026 with story-sized reviewed changes + monthly reviewed master->feature catch-up merges; merge changes carry the standard label gate (change 983874: Verified+2/CR+2/Workflow+1).
- Qt: reviewed merge changes live on codereview.qt-project.org (qt-creator origin/20.0->master merges June 2026); caveat: Qt abandoned ROUTINE cross-branch merges for release maintenance in 2020 (QUIP-16) in favor of cherry-picks — different use case (long-lived release branches) than finite feature branches.
- Wikimedia: ad-hoc merge commits into master confirmed; not documented policy.
- Chromium/AOSP/Go: deliberately linear (chains/topics/CQ) — the alternative school; their objection (merges hide interaction cost, hurt bisect) is the pattern's known weakness, mitigated by CI on the merge change.

## Three corrections vs assumptions
1. Human UI default diff base for merge commits is FIRST_PARENT (whole feature diff), not Auto Merge — auto-merge (conflict-resolutions-only) is a dropdown selection; server default confirmed in Gerrit source (GeneralPreferencesInfo.java). REST default IS auto-merge.
2. BOT TRAP: GET /changes/{id}/revisions/{rev}/patch on a merge commit returns HTTP 409 ("Revision has more than 1 parent", GetPatch.java); patch?parent=1 returns the ENTIRE feature diff (violates req 1). No /patch variant gives vs-auto-merge. The bot must branch on parent count and use files/ (no parent param => auto-merge base) + per-file /diff (auto-merge base) + /mergelist. TODAY our voter would 409 -> fail-closed -1 on any merge change (safe failure, but blocks the pattern).
3. Gerrit has a purpose-built changekind MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE ("don't want to trigger CI or human verification again if your target branch moved forward", config-labels.html): add to LLM-Review copyCondition so re-merging after main advances doesn't wipe the vote; a new feature-tip is a REWORK and correctly re-reviews.

## Scorecard (feature-branch pattern): req1 PASS (story diffs small; merge change reviews conflict-delta vs auto-merge; caveat: textually-clean semantic conflicts show EMPTY auto-merge diff — CI on the merge change is the mitigation => open epic smoky-flare-slug/1fa8 Verified vote becomes a required complement, not optional). req2 PASS (feature branches live only in Gerrit; replication pushes main+tags only). req3 PASS (submit requirement has no branch clause — already gates feature branches; every commit reaching main was gated as story change or merge change). req4 PASS (no rebases; votes consumed at story-merge; MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE is Gerrit-native + doc-sanctioned). req5 PASS (OpenDev documented + live; honest caveats recorded).

## RED/BLUE/GREEN replay under the pattern
RED: change A -> feature branch, +1, submit into branch. BLUE: change B likewise (parallel worktrees fine — both target the branch; MERGE_IF_NECESSARY merges siblings without rebase). GREEN: pulls branch (A+B in history), builds C, small review, submit. Merge change to main: usually near-empty auto-merge delta + mergelist + CI. Zero re-review of A/B/C. Zero vote wipes.

## Concrete deltas to implement
a. infra/gerrit/project.config: copyCondition = "changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE OR changekind:MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE"; [submit] explicit mergeContent=true + pin submitType=MERGE_IF_NECESSARY (currently unset/inherited — was already flagged); ACL: Create Reference + Delete Reference on refs/heads/feature/*; Push Merge Commit on refs/for/refs/heads/main + refs/for/refs/heads/feature/*.
b. src/rebar/review_bot/: merge-change code path (detect via revisions/{rev}/commit parents length; assemble review input from files/ + per-file diff vs auto-merge + mergelist; keep fail-closed).
c. keep receive.rejectImplicitMerges compatible (it does NOT block explicit merge commits — config-project-config.html).
d. CONTRIBUTING.md + docs: feature-branch workflow (OpenDev recipe incl. Change-Id amend), branch-lifetime cap, scheduled catch-up merges, branch deletion after merge-back (no Gerrit auto-cleanup exists).
e. smoky-flare-slug (CI Verified vote): elevate to required for merge changes (auto-merge diff cannot catch semantic conflicts).

comments.author: Iso Tester
comments.body:
COMPLETION-AWARE CONTAINER PLAN-REVIEW — brainstorm -> design -> decomposition -> signed plan-review PASS.

GOAL: turn placeholder epic 66ac (woozy-pea-kin) into a fully-defined, plan-reviewed, decomposable epic.

PROBLEM (refined during brainstorm): when the plan-review claim gate legitimately RE-FIRES on a
mid-flight container (epic reopened after a pause -> ADR 0009; or a material course-correction to the
epic plan), it reviews as if fresh and RE-LITIGATES acceptance criteria already delivered by
closed+attested children -> false BLOCKs + coaching to tighten shipped AC. The claim CASCADE is NOT a
driver (it only fires while the parent is `open`; an in_progress epic does not re-gate on further
child claims). Code-drift invalidation is INTENTIONAL and unchanged (a container's plan IS reviewed vs
codebase state — G6 runs at container scope): this epic changes only what a re-fired review DOES.

DECISION: option (b)/hybrid — completion-aware container review, keyed on VERIFIED delivery (the
signed completion attestation closed children already carry), never on bare `closed` status.

DESIGN (converged over ~10 turns, each grounded in prior art + adversarial subagent critique):
- Pass-1 stays completion-blind (full recall). A SEPARATE Pass-2 sub-call `plan_review_completion`
  (mirrors `plan_review_novelty`, passes.py:147) ALONE receives a delivered-children manifest and
  emits three atomic orthogonal sub-answers per finding, each a CLOSED enum with a keep-safe default:
  ATTRIBUTION (`<closed-child-id>` | none; STRUCTURAL for G3/G4 via `_container_child`, LLM+validated
  otherwise), CONTAINMENT (`limited-to-closed` | `spans-open-or-system` | `n-a`), LAYER
  (`plan-semantics` | `delivered-functionality` | `n-a`).
- Deterministic Pass-3 "completion floor" (third floor beside novelty ADR 0008 + drift-refresh
  ADR 0002) DROPS iff ALL: attribution=delivered-now child AND containment=limited-to-closed AND
  layer=plan-semantics AND priority<floor AND criterion NOT in the config-backed preserve-set
  (default T5c security / T10 contract). Every ambiguous value fails toward KEEP. Drops recorded to
  the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar with a distinct `drop_reason="completion"`; recomputed every run (a
  reopened/un-delivered child auto-resurfaces).
- `delivered-now`(child) = closed + VALID completion attestation (reuse the
  `compute_validity(...,'completion-verifier')` validity-on-read call — NOT the deficit-detector
  `_child_closure_findings` itself) OR superseded by a live in-epic SIBLING (structured `supersedes`
  link; direction B superseded_by A; A delivered-now or open/in_progress). Force-closed / abandoned /
  in-progress children are NOT delivered -> stay in scope. A parent reopen does NOT un-deliver
  children (ADR 0009 keys on each ticket's own last_reopened_at).

KEY EDGE DECISIONS: in-progress children stay FULLY in scope (v1). Force-close never trusted
(closes the laundering hole; the security/contract preserve-set is never dropped regardless of a
supersede edge). Sibling-supersede IN v1 (prevents the stale-closed-ticket hard-block Joe has
observed), sibling-verified. DEFERRED to separate epics: partial-completion attestation for
in-progress children; a structured `resolution` enum on `close`; the sidecar re-injection queue; an
optional second LAYER binary (calibration-gated).

PRIOR ART (why this is sound + why it is novel): NO prior art for scoped plan-quality review of a
partially-executed plan (LangGraph replan = regeneration not review; spec-kit /analyze =
completion-blind; incremental/delta verification = SAT not LLM) — benign gap (mainstream plans are
throwaway; rebar's signed, durable, verified-closed hierarchy is unusual). Suppression design
grounded in Tricorder/SonarQube/GitHub code-scanning (suppress on delivered+below-severity+
non-actionable, SEVERITY/SECURITY HARD VETO, never attribution-alone, never deletion); G-Eval/
CheckList/FLASK (few frozen atomic binaries + deterministic aggregation); ODC + IEEE-1028 (once
delivered, governing review shifts plan-review -> code-review; plan-semantics feedback goes moot,
delivered-substance stays live).

DECOMPOSITION (4 stories under 66ac, with file-impact + verify-commands + ordering deps):
- 6533 (reedy-hew-plume) Pass-3 completion floor + config evidence-gate + sidecar drop_reason + ADR 0020.
- 457a (tied-bulb-swoop) delivered-now predicate (validity-on-read reuse + sibling-supersede + reopen semantics).
- 94fd (tow-amok-jug) plan_review_completion Pass-2 sub-call + closed-enum contract + manifest assembler + degrade path.  depends_on 457a.
- 77cf (rag-yoke-clump) calibration gold-set (>=25 cases) + partially-complete-epic tests + reopen-resurface + close-op non-regression.  depends_on 6533, 94fd.
Ordering: 6533 depends_on 94fd + 457a; 77cf depends_on 6533 + 94fd; 94fd depends_on 457a.

OUTCOME: epic + 4 stories pass check-ac + clarity (7/5). `rebar review-plan 66ac` = PASS, blocking=0,
signed plan-review attestation certified at HEAD 49ad69b. Remediated across 4 rounds: 2 BLOCKs (name
the supersede artifact; fully enumerate the three sub-answer enums), all criticals (a real
`limited` vs `limited-to-closed` value-mismatch bug between 6533/94fd; the `_child_closure_findings`
deficit-detector inversion; missing sub-call output contract), and substantive majors (degrade path,
manifest owner, supersede signing rationale, determinism of attribution, reuse-vs-parallel, ADR 0020
+ cross-refs to 0008/0002, prompt-freeze-before-calibration, close-op non-regression). Residual: 5
sev=minor terminology/consistency advisories (severity-vs-priority wording, ADR-in-Scope, REVIEW_RESULT
naming) — triaged as diminishing-returns polish, not remediated further. NOT claimed/implemented —
this is the reviewed plan, ready to claim per-story.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
Design investigation: behavioral-comparison prompt + scope-drift protection for rebar's gates.

Findings (code): completion verifier (src/rebar/llm/completion.py + reviewers/completion_verifier.md) judges ticket vs pinned HEAD tree with read-only tools; it does NOT use commit trailers/file_impact/verify_commands for ticket<->code association. Gerrit review-bot reviews the diff in isolation: {{ticket_context}} prompt slots are filled with the DIFF (batch_runner.py:58, code-review.yaml:63-64); voter never extracts the rebar-ticket trailer or passes target_ticket, though produce_code_review_verdict accepts one and the attested tickets store is already materialized. verify-commit-ticket checks only that the id resolves — no content/status/claimant check. Net gap: no gate checks a diff semantically serves its named ticket; no scope-creep detection anywhere.

Research: Jin & Chen ASE 2025 (arXiv:2508.12358) — Behavioral Comparison Prompt (blind spec-summary + blind impl-summary, then compare) lifts correct-code recognition 52%->85-90%; rich single-pass judging (our current verifier shape) is the documented FP failure mode. BitsAI-CR: independent verify stage 25%->75% precision, conclusion-first output. Qodo/CodeRabbit: diff<->linked-ticket compliance is the production scope-check pattern; no published detector research — file_impact is a unique deterministic prior. Google Tricorder: advisory-first, ~10% not-useful demotion budget, blocking only for near-deterministic/execution-verified checks.

Proposal (4 parts): (1) restructure completion-verification.yaml into 3 steps — spec_summary (ticket only), impl_summary (code only, worklist = file_impact + trailer-linked paths, ticket prose withheld), compare (1-TURN conclusion-first); keep reconcile_verdict + signing unchanged. (2) Wire target_ticket into the Gerrit voter (extract_ticket_refs exists) + new advisory ticket-alignment LLM overlay + prompt-less DET files-outside-file_impact criterion in code_review/criteria_routing.json. (3) Asymmetric posture: under-delivery can FAIL (as today); over-delivery is advisory-only in v1, coach message names discovered_from/file_impact/AC-amend as the cure; scope amendments that only ADD file_impact should qualify for the drift_refresh lightweight re-sign path (attest.py) to avoid staling the plan-review attestation. Per-criterion noise budget (~10% override rate -> demote) before any blocking promotion. (4) Advisory ticket-status warning in verify-commit-ticket; untrailered commits not chased (completion verifier reads final tree, so correctness doesn't depend on trailer coverage).

Rollout: plumbing+DET -> behavioral-comparison verifier (eval before/after on eval_specs fixtures) -> ticket-alignment overlay advisory + telemetry -> earned per-criterion blocking.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: Completed a gap analysis comparing dso's LLM code review process (~/dso_code_review_report.md, extracted from digital-service-orchestra @ 2e9eaf4a44) against rebar's four-pass code-review gate. Full report written to ~/rebar_vs_dso_code_review_gap_report.md. Headline: adopt dso's calibration CONTENT (bug-anchored FP guards, absence-claim evidence obligations, verbatim cited excerpts, behavioral-testing standard, overlay concern checklists, rationalizations-to-reject) into rebar's STRUCTURE (find->verify->decide->coach kernel, deterministic severity arithmetic), plus dso's process loop (FP ledger -> bug-anchored guard -> eval case) and cross-patchset memory built on the kernel's existing novelty axis. Key detection gaps found in rebar: test-quality anti-patterns (dso's measured #1 FP/recall class), hallucinated-reference verification, deletion/asymmetric-change sweeps, AI-blindspot patterns (ui_artifacts, spaghetti patching, domain mismatch), ticket/AC scope checking, approach-viability signal, refactor-anomaly review. Key reliability gaps: DIFF_CHAR_CAP 60k silent truncation can still vote +1 (should be a coverage-gap), no eval specs for the 4-pass code-review prompts, no FP ledger, no cross-patchset finding memory. Explicitly preserved rebar's multi-pass design (deterministic verdict, narrow Pass-2, coach-not-block, enforcement-in-types) as superior to dso's prose-governed severity; dso's stale huge-diff prompt snapshots are the cautionary tale. Report ends with a 12-item prioritized roadmap.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
Compared DSO's planning-review criteria (~/dso_planning_criteria_report.md, digital-service-orchestra @ 2e9eaf4a44) against rebar's plan-review gate (docs/plan-review-gate.md, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/). Full report written to ~/dso_rebar_plan_review_gap_report.md and published as a claude.ai Artifact (https://claude.ai/code/artifact/a3f2069a-e882-4aa0-99be-bca19ed81b4d).

Method: 3 subagents extracted DSO's 8 source clusters (criteria, rubrics, FP filters, prompt engineering, reliability practices); 1 subagent mapped rebar's gate end-to-end (DET floor P1-P9, 4-pass find/verify/decide/coach, 32 LLM criteria, attestation mechanics, overlay surface). Synthesis preserves rebar's multi-pass severity-free-finder + typed-binary-verifier + deterministic-decide architecture as intentionally superior (DSO's own bug history — untrusted self-scored status fields, score inflation, skipped gates — validates it).

Key gaps identified (DSO catches, rebar doesn't): G-1 no conflict detection between findings (DSO's add_vs_remove/more_vs_less/strict_vs_flexible/expand_vs_reduce taxonomy); G-2 no oscillation detection across re-review rounds (sidecar norm_id history enables it); G-3 verify-command defect taxonomy (9 patterns) + behavioral-command blacklist (grep/ls/cat/test -f = file inspection, not behavior); G-4 OUT-assertion / scope-exclusion false preconditions; G-5 behavioral-prohibition consumer scan (call sites of newly-forbidden behavior); G-6 in-flight cross-ticket interaction scanning (file_impact intersection + 4-tier semantic classification); G-7 requirement-provenance / inference-signal lexicon when no session log linked; G-8 T3 command-surface empiricism (per-command --help, endpoint granularity, env preconditions); G-9 scale grounding + upward-interpolation prohibition; G-10 CI-trigger/release-infra coverage audit; G-11 G3 three-part coverage standard + bypass-annotation patterns; G-12 prompt-injection directive missing from reviewer prompts.

FP-avoidance transfers to Pass 2: new verifier binary respects_artifact_altitude (findings presuming choices the artifact legitimately defers); restatement gloss on no_existing_mitigation; already-standard-practice check in codebase-grounded guards; ambiguity-not-absence framing (T5c/T10); one-way blast-radius ratchet.

Reliability: measure chunk co-residency contamination for the blocking seven via sidecar (R-1); double-verification agreement for block-crossing findings (R-2); document asymmetric-error directions as design invariants (R-3); bug-history citations in rubrics (R-4); registry-generated authoring companion doc (R-5); pink-elephant/affirmative-framing audit of packaged prompts (R-6).
